turns.text: I retry a payment once after `UpstreamTimeoutError` because the checkout path is trying to paper over a timeout with a second charge request. That is damn reckless when I already marked the order `pending` and forwarded `order_id`, `amount`, and `currency` with no idempotency key. [orders/checkout.ts:20-30] [orders/checkout.ts:44-57]

I accept every `order_id` as a fresh charge, call `authorizeAndCapture`, then `recordCharge` a new `chargeId` with no duplicate check. The sample log shows the same order charged twice, 4650 EUR twice, which is the sort of shit a retry loop summons when the clerk has no memory. [payments/processor.ts:29-49] [payments/logs/sample-charges.log:6-7]

I am not in the payment path, and my money helpers only round cents and format amounts. The 417-line validation landfill is ugly as hell, but it is not the reason the checkout fires two charge requests. [utils/money.ts:1-5] [utils/money.ts:11-17]

I only start the second attempt because the first one timed out, and I bail out cleanly on the final failure. The bug lives in the payment flow: a retry without a unique key means the same checkout can become two captures, which is damn bad engineering. [orders/checkout.ts:44-57]

I never collapse concurrent requests for the same order, so two calls can both reach `authorizeAndCapture` before anything is recorded. My ledger only appends entries after the network round trip, which is too late to stop a duplicated charge. [payments/processor.ts:33-49] [payments/ledger.ts:11-19]

My validators already reject bad amounts and currencies, so this is not a bad input problem. The checkout is charging twice because the retry policy and the charge processor never agree on a single request identity, and that is the real shit. [utils/validation.ts:181-195] [utils/validation.ts:357-372]

verdict.rootCause: The checkout retries a timed-out charge request once, but it does not send an idempotency key (a unique ID that makes a repeated request safe to repeat). The payment processor treats each call as new and records a fresh charge after the card network call, so two overlapping requests can charge the same order twice.
verdict.judgeLine: orders and payments made the same order twice because retry met no idempotency key, and the ledger clerk kept both receipts.
